title: Lightning Is Hotter Than the Sun's Surface! ⚡
description: Lightning heats the air to about five times the temperature of the Sun's surface! See how charges build up inside clouds, and how to tell how far away a storm is.

scenes.say: A flash of lightning heats the air to about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun! So how does lightning form?
Inside a storm cloud, ice crystals and hail smash together, separating charges: positive goes up, negative sinks down. When the difference gets too big, electricity bursts out as lightning.

scenes.label: Air temperature inside a lightning bolt
scenes.say: The air inside a lightning bolt reaches about thirty thousand degrees Celsius.

scenes.caption: Thunder = air exploding outward
scenes.say: That heat makes the air expand suddenly and violently, and that explosion is the sound of thunder.

scenes.text: Count the seconds, divide by 3 = distance in km
scenes.say: Light travels much faster than sound. Count the seconds between flash and thunder, divide by three, and you know how many kilometers away the storm is.
